The configuration allows you to adapt the examination of the files very individually to the respective situation (examination of C files is currently not available). Detailed information about the way of scanning and parsing your source files is explained in this page.

para.text: In the context of "ToDo Grid" a
ToDo is any individual text within the source code that complies with the following rules. To

text.style: font-family:Verdana; font-size:10pt; font-weight:normal; font-style:normal; text-decoration:none; text-transform:none; vertical-align:baseline; color:#000000; background-color:transparent; letter-spacing:normal; letter-scaling:100%;

para.text: separate this text from the code to be compiled, the text is marked as a comment. You can use // for single line ToDo and (* *) or { } for multi line ToDo.

text.style: font-family:Verdana; font-size:10pt; font-weight:normal; font-style:normal; text-decoration:none; text-transform:none; vertical-align:baseline; color:#000000; background-color:transparent; letter-spacing:normal; letter-scaling:100%;

para.text: After the start of the comment section, an inserted keyword (token) identifies and specifies the following text. The definition of the token is essentially free; however, if you're working within a group of programmers, there will be rules that must be observed. Thanks to the ability to individually activate / deactivate the tokens to be considered for scanning, adaptation to the specific work situation is very easy.

table.style: width:100%; border-width:0px; border-spacing:0px; border-collapse:collapse; cell-border-width:1px; border-color:#000000; border-style:solid;

para.text: Of course, the entries can be entered manually, but it is faster if you use pre-made templates. To insert pre-made entries, you can use the "source code templates" available in the IDE, which can be accessed via Ctrl+J. Alternatively, you can also use the "Code Librarian" expert. In both cases, regular ToDo texts must be created first, which can then be quickly inserted later.
In a multi line ToDo, the token should be placed on the line where the comment begins.

text.style: font-family:Verdana; font-size:10pt; font-weight:normal; font-style:normal; text-decoration:none; text-transform:none; vertical-align:baseline; color:#000000; background-color:transparent; letter-spacing:normal; letter-scaling:100%;

para.text: The number of lines read and evaluated in a multi line ToDo is limited; no more than 5 lines should be used.

In order to keep the time required for scanning the files as short as possible, ToDo that are no longer needed should also be removed from the source - a perhaps unspectacular task, but one that should nevertheless be carried out regularly (even within a working group)!

The following rules are intended as a general background, which can be consulted if the scan results do not meet your expectations. With individual use, a personal approach will quickly develop, so that these comprehensive rules will be followed almost automatically. However, it's definitely worth reading through ...

table.style: width:100%; border-width:0px; border-spacing:0px; border-collapse:collapse; cell-border-width:1px; border-color:#000000; border-style:solid;

para.text: The scan function of "ToDo Grid" allows a large number of structural variations of the ToDo entries. This is particularly important when editing external source code whose formatting cannot be sufficiently influenced.
In general, ToDo entries should be as short and clear as possible. No long texts should be stored here, it is recommended to use single-line ToDo entries.

list.style: text-align:justify; margin-top:12px; margin-right:6px; margin-left:6px; font-family:Wingdings; font-size:10pt; color:#000000;

li.text: The simplest ToDo entry consists of a token and a description text, for example:

list.style: text-align:justify; margin-top:3px; margin-right:6px; margin-bottom:3px; margin-left:6px; font-family:Wingdings; font-size:8pt; color:#000000;

li.text: Spaces may be inserted between the comment introduction and the token, but it is recommended not to do so

li.text: recognized case-sensitive. As already mentioned, the definition of tokens is essentially free (this is done in the configuration). However, if you're working within a group of programmers, there will be rules that must be observed.

li.text: between token and text can be done by spaces or a colon. Multiple spaces are allowed, but for space reasons, this should not be overdone. If a number is at the beginning of the description text, it
be separated by a colon (otherwise the number will be considered as priority).

li.text: should be as short and concise as possible. If the scan does not find a description in an otherwise valid ToDo entry, the message "No description found" is displayed in the string grid.

li.text: More complex ToDo can optionally contain additional categories and owners, for example:

li.text: Of course, each parameter can be specified alone. The

parameter. Any number of (or no) spaces can be inserted before, between, and after the parameters. To ensure good readability, it is recommended to insert a space before, between and after the parameters.

li.text: are generally freely definable, but may not contain any spaces or hyphens and must be placed immediately after the parameter. For ease of analysis, the definition set of categories and owners should be as small as possible.

li.text: The application optionally provides the ability to assign category and owner to a token (see configuration). In case of a
between the term used in the source and the token assignment, the term used in the source is displayed in the string grid.

list.style: text-align:justify; margin-top:3px; margin-right:6px; margin-bottom:3px; margin-left:6px; font-family:Wingdings; font-size:8pt; color:#000000;

li.text: If the parameters -c and -o are specified multiple times, only the first occurrence is evaluated; the order of the two parameters is not relevant.

list.style: text-align:justify; margin-top:12px; margin-right:6px; margin-left:6px; font-family:Wingdings; font-size:10pt; color:#000000;

li.text: Last but not least, each ToDo entry can be given a priority.

list.style: text-align:justify; margin-top:3px; margin-right:6px; margin-bottom:3px; margin-left:6px; font-family:Wingdings; font-size:8pt; color:#000000;

li.text: can be specified by a single-digit number after the token. There must be one or more spaces between the token and the number. If there is no space between the token and the number, the number is considered part of the token. It is recommended to add a space before and after the number.

list.style: text-align:justify; margin-top:3px; margin-right:6px; margin-bottom:3px; margin-left:6px; font-family:Wingdings; font-size:8pt; color:#000000;

li.text: declared by the application. The digits 0 and 6..9 are mapped to 5, which means "Lowest" priority.

li.text: The application optionally provides the ability to assign a priority to a token (see configuration). In case of a
between the value used in the source and the token assignment, the value used in the source is displayed in the string grid.
